research.title: Shifting Work Patterns with Generative AI
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and organization; 6-month, cross-industry randomized field experiment with 6,000 knowledge workers
research.finding: Access to AI changed work that individuals could change independently, including less time spent on email and moderately faster document completion. It did not significantly change time spent in meetings, a coordination-dependent activity.
research.impact: Strengthen separate measurement of individual throughput and coordination outcomes. Reject productivity change as a proxy for improved collaboration.
research.boundary: The report describes access and work-pattern effects, not the quality, safety, or persistence of cross-repository coordination. Next: which repeated-use measures observe handoff quality, correction, and ownership changes rather than only time use?
research.flags: working paper; coordination outcome coverage limited

research.title: Generative AI at Work
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and organization; staggered deployment study of 5,172 customer-support agents
research.finding: AI assistance increased issues resolved per hour by about 15% on average, with larger gains for less experienced and lower-skilled workers. The highest-skilled group saw smaller gains and some quality decline.
research.impact: Strengthen expertise-sensitive baselines and distributional reporting. Reject one average productivity effect as a routing rule.
research.boundary: One support setting with a purpose-built assistant does not establish transfer to open-ended work. Next: when does AI diffuse expert practice without flattening expert judgment?
research.flags: selection and rollout confounding; support-work domain

research.title: The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and organization; three randomized field experiments covering 4,867 developers
research.finding: Pooled results associated coding-assistant access with a 26.08% increase in completed tasks, with higher adoption and gains among less experienced developers.
research.impact: Watch as counterevidence to 022. Strengthen context, experience, adoption, and task-mix reporting.
research.boundary: The experiments are noisy individually, use completed-task measures, and do not resolve code quality or long-term maintenance. Next: which design differences explain the opposite productivity directions in 022 and 023?
research.design: Preprint, three enterprise developer field experiments
research.flags: preprint; pooled organization and adoption effects

research.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
research.levelEvidence: Workflow; randomized controlled trial with 16 experienced developers and 246 tasks in mature open-source repositories
research.finding: Allowing AI tools increased completion time by 19%, even though participants expected and later believed that AI made them faster.
research.impact: Strengthen observed-versus-perceived outcome checks. Reject self-reported speed as evaluation evidence.
research.boundary: The sample is small, unusually experienced, and limited to early-2025 tools and familiar repositories. Next: which task and familiarity features predict when assistance becomes overhead?
research.design: Practitioner report of randomized mature-repository trial
research.flags: small participant count; early-2025 tools; open-source setting

research.title: Scaffolding Human-AI Collaboration: A Field Experiment on Behavioral Protocols and Cognitive Reframing
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and organization; field experiment with 388 employees at a Fortune 500 retailer
research.finding: A structured pair-use protocol was associated with lower document quality and substantially lower document production than unstructured use. A cognitive framing intervention was associated with higher individual quality at the top of the distribution, subject to reported design limitations.
research.impact: Watch protocol and framing interventions. Reject structure alone as evidence of better collaboration. No runtime change.
research.boundary: This is a preprint with an AM/PM session confound, differential attrition, and LLM-grading sensitivity to document length. Next: can a preregistered, replicated field study show durable benefit without reducing throughput?

research.title: The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI and Teamwork
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and organization; preregistered field experiment with 791 professionals working on real product-innovation challenges
research.finding: Individuals with AI matched teams without AI on average solution quality, while the study's decomposition found that AI improved idea generation and human teams retained an advantage in evaluative selection.
research.impact: Watch role-specific collaboration hypotheses. Strengthen stage-specific outcome measurement instead of a single collaboration score.
research.boundary: This is a one-day organizational experiment, not evidence of durable teamwork or authority transfer. Next: can repeated-use studies preserve human evaluative selection while testing whether AI-assisted generation remains beneficial over time?

research.title: Collaborating with AI Agents: Field Experiments on Teamwork, Productivity, and Performance
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and organization; marketing experiment with 2,310 participants, randomized agent traits, and downstream campaign tests
research.finding: Human-AI teams increased communication and some text productivity, but human-human teams produced stronger images and overall campaign results were similar. Trait pairing changed outcomes in both directions.
research.impact: Watch participant and modality fit. Strengthen disaggregated outcome and coordination-cost measurement.
research.boundary: This is a preprint in a marketing setting with platform-specific interventions. Next: can a matched evaluation identify when another agent changes the result rather than only increasing messages and cost?

research.title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
research.levelEvidence: Task; preregistered experiment with 453 professionals completing short writing tasks
research.finding: ChatGPT access reduced completion time by about 40% and raised rated output quality by about 18%, while compressing performance differences between participants.
research.impact: Strengthen matched time-and-quality measurement. Watch skill compression and task-boundary effects.
research.boundary: The tasks were short, self-contained, and text based. Next: do gains survive multi-stage work with persistent context, verification, and accountability?
research.flags: short writing tasks; no maintenance outcome

research.title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier
research.levelEvidence: Task and workflow; preregistered field experiment with 758 consultants across tasks inside and outside an AI capability frontier
research.finding: AI improved speed and quality on tasks within its capability frontier, but reduced correctness on a task outside that frontier even when the tasks appeared similarly difficult.
research.impact: Strengthen capability-boundary detection and task-specific evaluation. Reject provider-level capability claims as sufficient routing evidence.
research.boundary: The frontier was constructed for one model, occupation, and task set. Next: how can a workflow detect boundary crossings before an apparently competent output becomes authoritative?
research.flags: one occupation; frontier defined by tested model and tasks

research.title: When combinations of humans and AI are useful: A systematic review and meta-analysis
research.levelEvidence: Task and interaction; preregistered systematic review and meta-analysis of 106 experiments and 370 effect sizes
research.finding: On average, human-AI combinations performed worse than the better human-only or AI-only baseline. Effects varied: decision-making tasks showed losses, content-creation tasks showed gains, and augmentation depended on which side initially performed better.
research.impact: Strengthen matched baseline evaluation. Reject any general claim that adding AI creates synergy.
research.boundary: The reviewed evidence is experimental and heterogeneous, with possible publication bias and differing study designs. Next: which coordination mechanisms improve the best-baseline comparison in sustained, privacy-constrained work?
research.design: Journal preregistered systematic review and meta-analysis
research.flags: heterogeneous tasks and interventions; publication bias possible

research.title: Human-generative AI collaboration enhances task performance but undermines human’s intrinsic motivation
research.levelEvidence: Task and short-sequence interaction; four preregistered online experiments with 3,562 participants
research.finding: GenAI assistance improved the assisted task, but did not establish a lasting independent-performance benefit. In several collaboration-to-solo comparisons, intrinsic motivation fell and boredom rose more than in solo-only sequences.
research.impact: Watch continuity and agency effects. Strengthen separate outcome, burden, and post-handoff measures.
research.boundary: Professional-role simulations and short task sequences do not establish durable workplace effects. Next: how should a protocol distinguish a useful handoff from a reliance pattern that leaves later independent work worse?

research.title: How human-AI feedback loops alter human perceptual, emotional and social judgements
research.levelEvidence: Interaction and repeated judgment; experiments with 1,401 participants across perceptual, emotional, and social domains
research.finding: Repeated interaction with biased AI altered human judgments and amplified bias more than comparable human interaction. Participants often underestimated the AI influence.
research.impact: Strengthen correction, counterevidence, and independence checks. Reject passive repeated exposure as a safe reliance model.
research.boundary: Judgment tasks and selected algorithms do not map directly to repository work. Next: which correction and provenance signals reduce feedback-loop effects in sustained, open-ended collaboration?

research.title: Human-AI Collaboration via Conditional Delegation: A Case Study of Content Moderation
research.levelEvidence: Task and delegation; randomized study across in-distribution and out-of-distribution content-moderation settings
research.finding: Human-authored rules could identify useful delegation regions in the studied setting, but creating reliable rules became harder under distribution shift and explanations did not guarantee better performance.
research.impact: Watch bounded conditional delegation for stable, observable regions. Strengthen distribution-shift checks before reusing a rule.
research.boundary: The work uses relatively low-stakes keyword moderation and an experimental interface. Next: can delegation rules remain legible and safe in open-ended workflows with changing models?
research.flags: preprint; content-moderation labels; induced distribution shift

research.title: Updates in Human-AI Teams: Understanding and Addressing the Performance/Compatibility Tradeoff
research.levelEvidence: Task and continuity; model-update experiments in AI-advised decision settings
research.finding: A more accurate model update can reduce team performance when its new errors violate the human participant's learned expectations.
research.impact: Strengthen version-change compatibility and revalidation. Reject higher model accuracy as sufficient evidence that an established workflow improved.
research.boundary: The experiments use structured classification decisions. Next: which model, prompt, tool, and policy changes should invalidate prior delegation and reliance evidence?

research.title: Roles of Artificial Intelligence in Collaboration with Humans: Automation, Augmentation, and the Future of Work
research.levelEvidence: Task; analytical allocation model validated with experimental image-classification data
research.finding: Automation, augmentation, and human-only work are task-allocation choices. Their value depends on between-task and within-task complementarity, task difficulty, and the ability to reallocate human effort.
research.impact: Test as a candidate capability: evidence-based work allocation. Do not convert it into a universal routing rule.
research.boundary: The experiment uses idealized judgment tasks with known ground truth. Next: which non-performance factors, including consequence, accountability, and privacy, must constrain allocation?

research.title: Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance
research.levelEvidence: Task and interaction; mixed-method user studies across three datasets
research.finding: AI assistance produced some complementary performance, but explanations did not increase it. Explanations increased acceptance of recommendations whether they were right or wrong.
research.impact: Reject explanation presence as a proxy for collaboration quality. Strengthen separate measurement of human-only, AI-only, and team outcomes.
research.boundary: The tasks were bounded classification and reasoning tasks. Next: which outcome set captures quality, effort, reversibility, and accountability in open-ended work?

research.title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-Assisted Decision-Making
research.levelEvidence: Task and interaction; experiment with 199 participants
research.finding: Cognitive-forcing interventions reduced overreliance more than simple explanation interfaces, but the strongest interventions received the least favorable subjective ratings and effects varied with need for cognition.
research.impact: Strengthen deliberate review at consequential boundaries. Test proportionate friction rather than adding a universal interruption.
research.boundary: One experimental task does not establish the right intervention for sustained professional work. Next: what is the least disruptive intervention that improves error detection for a given consequence level?

research.title: Beyond Accuracy: The Role of Mental Models in Human-AI Team Performance
research.levelEvidence: Task and interaction; controlled experiments on AI-advised classification
research.finding: Team performance depends partly on whether people can form a usable mental model of the AI's error boundary, which is affected by task complexity and error predictability.
research.impact: Strengthen capability-boundary legibility. Reject aggregate accuracy as evidence that a participant can anticipate when to rely.
research.boundary: Controlled classification tasks do not capture open-ended tool use or authority. Next: what minimal capability statement remains accurate after configuration and version changes?

research.title: Is the Most Accurate AI the Best Teammate? Optimizing AI for Teamwork
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; expected-team-utility modeling and experiments on high-stakes datasets
research.finding: Predictable performance can be worth a small loss in stand-alone accuracy when final decision quality, verification cost, human skill, and mistake cost are considered.
research.impact: Watch team utility as an analysis aid. Reject collapsing Breadcrumbs' separate quality, burden, authority, and recovery measures into one score.
research.boundary: The utility model assumes a structured accept-or-solve interaction. Next: which variables can inform a decision without becoming a universal optimization target?
research.design: Conference formal team-utility modeling plus experiments

research.title: Algorithm Aversion: People Erroneously Avoid Algorithms After Seeing Them Err
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; five incentivized forecasting studies
research.finding: Participants lost confidence in an algorithm faster than in a human after observing comparable mistakes, even when the algorithm performed better.
research.impact: Strengthen matched error-history presentation. Reject adoption rate as performance evidence.
research.boundary: Forecasting choices do not cover open-ended work. Next: how should systems show comparative failure rates without encouraging blanket reliance?
research.design: Journal series of incentivized forecasting experiments

research.title: Overcoming Algorithm Aversion: People Will Use Imperfect Algorithms If They Can (Even Slightly) Modify Them
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; three incentivized forecasting studies
research.finding: Limited ability to modify algorithmic forecasts increased use and improved performance, apparently by restoring some control.
research.impact: Watch bounded editability and contestability. Reject user control as evidence that the combined result is accurate or fair.
research.boundary: Numeric forecasting with restricted edits is narrower than repository work. Next: which edits improve correction without creating untraceable overrides?
research.flags: limited numeric edits; use is not correctness

research.title: Algorithm Appreciation: People Prefer Algorithmic to Human Judgment
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; six advice-taking experiments
research.finding: Lay participants often weighted algorithmic advice more than human advice, but appreciation weakened when comparing advice with their own judgment and among experienced forecasters.
research.impact: Strengthen expertise and comparison-frame controls. Reject algorithm aversion as a universal behavior.
research.boundary: The tasks center on estimates and forecasts. Next: when does appreciation become overreliance in open-ended work?

research.title: Task-Dependent Algorithm Aversion
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; four laboratory and two field studies
research.finding: Reliance on algorithms was lower for tasks perceived as subjective, and task framing changed perceived objectivity and use.
research.impact: Strengthen task-characteristic reporting. Reject adoption differences as direct evidence of capability.
research.boundary: Consumer decisions and marketing interventions may not transfer to professional accountability. Next: which task properties predict appropriate, not merely increased, reliance?
research.flags: consumer and marketing settings; framing sensitivity

research.title: Disparate Interactions: An Algorithm-in-the-Loop Analysis of Fairness in Risk Assessments
research.levelEvidence: Decision and sociotechnical system; controlled risk-assessment experiment
research.finding: Participants underperformed the risk model, could not reliably judge performance, and interacted with advice in racially disparate ways.
research.impact: Strengthen subgroup and interaction-effect evaluation. Reject fair stand-alone model metrics as proof of a fair combined system.
research.boundary: Lay simulations do not establish judge behavior. Next: which workflow traces reveal disparate interaction before deployment?

research.title: Algorithmic Risk Assessments Can Alter Human Decision-Making Processes in High-Stakes Government Contexts
research.levelEvidence: Decision and policy; experiment with 2,140 participants across pretrial and loan contexts
research.finding: Risk advice changed how participants weighted risk, increasing detention disparity in one setting and reducing aid in another, despite potential predictive gains.
research.impact: Strengthen value-shift and policy-outcome checks. Reject prediction accuracy as sufficient decision quality.
research.boundary: Simulated government decisions do not prove field effects. Next: how can a workflow detect when advice changes the objective being optimized?
research.design: Journal experiment across pretrial and loan contexts

research.title: Manipulating and Measuring Model Interpretability
research.levelEvidence: Task and interaction; preregistered experiments with 3,800 participants
research.finding: Simpler transparent models improved simulation of predictions but did not increase beneficial following and reduced detection of large model mistakes in one condition.
research.impact: Strengthen behavioral interpretability tests. Reject transparency or simulability as automatic error-correction evidence.
research.boundary: Synthetic prediction tasks do not cover all explanation goals. Next: which explanation improves a named decision behavior without information overload?

research.title: Interpreting Interpretability: Understanding Data Scientists' Use of Interpretability Tools for Machine Learning
research.levelEvidence: Workflow; study of data scientists using GAM and SHAP tools
research.finding: Practitioners used interpretability tools in varied, sometimes overconfident ways and could draw unwarranted conclusions from tool outputs.
research.impact: Strengthen interpretation training, caveats, and misuse tests. Reject tool availability as proof of understanding.
research.boundary: Data-science workflows differ from general agent use. Next: which caveats change behavior rather than become ignored boilerplate?
research.design: Conference user study of interpretability tools

research.title: Generative AI Enhances Individual Creativity but Reduces the Collective Diversity of Novel Content
research.levelEvidence: Task and collective output; preregistered story-writing experiment
research.finding: AI assistance improved individual ratings, especially for less creative writers, while making outputs more similar to each other.
research.impact: Strengthen portfolio-diversity measurement. Reject average item quality as sufficient collective value.
research.boundary: Short creative-writing tasks do not establish organizational innovation effects. Next: when does repeated model assistance narrow the research or design portfolio?

research.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and implementation; framework description plus pilot applications across several domains
research.finding: Configurable agents, tools, human input, and conversation patterns can compose multi-agent applications. The paper demonstrates feasibility and flexibility, not a general advantage over one agent or proof of governance.
research.impact: Watch as implementation evidence. Do not promote conversational multiplicity into a coordination principle or performance claim.
research.boundary: Pilot applications do not isolate when extra agents help, duplicate work, or amplify error. Next: what matched evaluation distinguishes coordination benefit from added calls and shared context?

research.title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
research.levelEvidence: Task and workflow; controlled evaluation of 180 single-agent and multi-agent configurations across four agentic benchmarks and three model families
research.finding: Multi-agent systems helped parallelizable work but degraded sequential planning by 39% to 70%. Independent agents amplified errors more than centralized systems, and tool density increased coordination cost.
research.impact: Strengthen task-decomposability and error-containment checks. Reject agent count as a quality proxy.
research.boundary: Benchmark architectures and tasks do not prove the same effects in governed repository work. Next: can a bounded owning-system test predict when centralized delegation beats one agent?
research.design: Industry research benchmark across agent configurations
research.flags: benchmark transfer; configuration selection; judge dependence

research.title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM agents
research.levelEvidence: Task and interaction; benchmark across six interactive scenarios, multiple coordination topologies, and milestone-based indicators
research.finding: Coordination topology and planning strategy changed milestone progress and task results. A graph topology performed best in one research scenario, while cognitive planning improved milestone achievement by 3%.
research.impact: Watch milestone and topology measures. Reject transfer of one topology result into a default architecture.
research.boundary: Simulated scenarios and model-specific rankings do not establish operational superiority. Next: which milestone signals remain meaningful in real handoffs with authority and privacy boundaries?
research.flags: scenario and topology dependence; no mature-repository field test

research.title: AI Agents That Matter
research.levelEvidence: Ecosystem and evaluation; critical analysis plus cost-aware benchmark optimization
research.finding: Accuracy-only evaluation can reward complex, expensive agents, obscure the source of gains, and encourage benchmark overfitting. Downstream users and model developers also need different evaluation evidence.
research.impact: Strengthen joint cost-and-outcome evaluation, holdouts, and downstream-fit reporting.
research.boundary: This is a methodological critique, not a field test of one collaboration workflow. Next: what minimum holdout and replay design prevents Breadcrumbs patterns from overfitting their own examples?
research.design: Preprint critical analysis plus cost-aware benchmark work

research.title: Beyond Prompts: Dynamic Conversational Benchmarking of Large Language Models
research.levelEvidence: Interaction and workflow; synthetic long-conversation benchmark with interleaved tasks and context switching
research.finding: Models that performed well on isolated tasks struggled when those tasks were interleaved. Long-term-memory augmentation sometimes matched or exceeded larger context windows.
research.impact: Strengthen interleaving and recovery tests. Reject context-window size as continuity evidence.
research.boundary: Synthetic conversations do not reproduce repository authority or real user stakes. Next: can fresh-session evaluation separate retrieval success from correct task ownership and stale-context rejection?

research.title: Seeing the Whole Elephant: A Benchmark for Failure Attribution in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and evaluation; 220 annotated failure traces from three agentic systems
research.finding: Full execution traces improved agent-level and step-level failure attribution over output-only evidence. The benchmark attributes failure to the missed recovery responsibility when an upstream mistake remained correctable.
research.impact: Strengthen complete trace capture and recovery-aware responsibility. Reject final-output inspection as sufficient incident evidence.
research.boundary: Attribution accuracy remains limited and varies by architecture and trace completeness. Next: which minimum trace fields support reliable correction without retaining unnecessary private content?
research.design: Conference benchmark of 220 annotated agent failure traces
research.flags: trace sampling and annotator dependence; benchmark systems

research.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
research.levelEvidence: Task, tool use, and security; dynamic environment with 97 realistic tasks and 629 security test cases
research.finding: Tool-using agents failed many ordinary tasks and remained vulnerable to prompt injection from untrusted tool data. Security and task utility must be evaluated together.
research.impact: Strengthen instruction-data separation and adversarial evaluation. Reject successful tool execution as evidence of safe delegation.
research.boundary: The benchmark is simulated and cannot enumerate future attacks. Next: how should a governed workflow preserve provenance and authority when retrieved content contains instructions?
research.flags: simulated content and tools; defense coverage changes quickly

research.title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
research.levelEvidence: Task and evaluation; multi-domain benchmark with partially observable, multi-turn environments and process-level analytics
research.finding: Final success rate hides partial progress and failure location. AgentBoard adds a progress-rate measure and process views across multiple agent environments.
research.impact: Strengthen stage and progress evidence. Reject completion status as the only workflow measure.
research.boundary: Benchmark progress does not itself capture human authority, burden, or recovery. Next: which process milestones should be standardized without creating a misleading composite score?

research.title: OSWORLD: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
research.levelEvidence: Task and tool use; executable benchmark of 369 open-ended tasks across real desktop applications and operating systems
research.finding: Humans completed 72.4% of tasks while the best evaluated agents completed less than 12.2%, exposing major grounding and operational-knowledge gaps in realistic computer use.
research.impact: Strengthen executable-environment validation and bounded authority. Reject fluent planning as evidence of reliable computer action.
research.boundary: Models and systems have advanced since the study, and benchmark success is not deployment safety. Next: what current, owning-system test is required before a computer-use capability receives write authority?
research.flags: environment and model versions age quickly

research.title: Learning to Complement Humans
research.levelEvidence: Task and allocation; team-optimized learning evaluated in scientific-discovery and medical-diagnosis settings
research.finding: Optimizing a model for the combined human-machine result can outperform optimizing the model alone when human error patterns are known.
research.impact: Watch complementary-error allocation as a candidate evaluation. Reject stand-alone model accuracy as the only routing signal.
research.boundary: The tasks are structured and depend on labeled or estimable human behavior. Next: how can complementary error regions be estimated without profiling people beyond the owning workflow's need?
research.design: Preprint formal team-optimization work plus experiments

research.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
research.levelEvidence: Memory and continuity; 500 curated questions embedded in scalable interaction histories
research.finding: Long-term memory requires information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention. Evaluated systems showed substantial degradation across sustained interactions.
research.impact: Strengthen update, temporal, and abstention tests in the memory exam. Reject recall accuracy or context length as sufficient memory evidence.
research.boundary: The histories and questions are benchmark constructs and do not test authority, provenance, or repository custody. Next: how should correction survival and source precedence be evaluated alongside these abilities?
research.flags: generated histories; benchmark and model-judge dependence

research.title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
research.levelEvidence: Memory and continuity; human-edited generated dialogues averaging 600 turns and 16,000 tokens across up to 32 sessions
research.finding: Long-context models and retrieval improved some results but still lagged humans on long-range temporal and causal understanding, question answering, event summaries, and multimodal dialogue.
research.impact: Strengthen causal, temporal, and multi-session evaluation. Reject a large context window as proof of durable memory.
research.boundary: The conversations are generated and edited rather than operational records. Next: which failures persist when the source of truth is versioned repository evidence?
research.flags: generated and human-edited dialogues; no repository custody

research.title: MemBench: Towards More Comprehensive Evaluation on the Memory of LLM-based Agents
research.levelEvidence: Memory and evaluation; benchmark spanning factual and reflective memory, participation and observation, effectiveness, efficiency, and capacity
research.finding: Memory evaluation changes materially by memory level, interaction role, and resource dimension. One recall measure cannot represent the capability.
research.impact: Strengthen multi-dimensional memory evaluation and participant-versus-observer distinctions. Reject one memory score.
research.boundary: The benchmark does not evaluate governance, cross-context isolation, correction authority, or repository ownership. Next: which governance dimensions can be added without obscuring benchmark performance?
research.flags: benchmark construct choices; no governance evaluation

research.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
research.levelEvidence: Memory architecture; virtual-context design demonstrated on document analysis and multi-session chat
research.finding: Explicit memory tiers and control flow can move information between limited active context and external storage.
research.impact: Watch tiered context and explicit control-flow patterns. Reject storage movement as proof of truth, provenance, retention policy, or authority.
research.boundary: The paper demonstrates an architecture and benchmark applications, not a governed memory system. Next: what evidence must accompany every move between context tiers?
research.flags: builder-evaluated; architecture demo; no authority semantics

research.title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
research.levelEvidence: Memory architecture; retrieval, summarization, update, and forgetting mechanisms evaluated with simulated users and qualitative dialogue
research.finding: A long-term conversation system can retrieve, summarize, update, and selectively retain interaction-derived information.
research.impact: Watch explicit update and retention evaluation. Reject an anthropomorphic forgetting curve as a sufficient retention or deletion policy.
research.boundary: Companion-style interactions and simulated evaluation do not establish correction, consent, or governance. Next: which retention changes require an owning-system rule or human decision?

research.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
research.levelEvidence: Memory, reflection, and planning; 25 simulated agents plus ablations and human believability ratings
research.finding: An observation stream, retrieval, reflection, and planning produced more believable simulated behavior than ablated variants.
research.impact: Watch reflection-linked retrieval and planning as an implementation pattern. Reject believability as evidence of factual correctness or workflow benefit.
research.boundary: The target was simulated social believability, not truth, authority, or professional task performance. Next: which reflection outputs can be checked against source evidence before reuse?
research.design: Conference simulated-agent study with human ratings
research.flags: simulation; believability outcome; model-judge and rater dependence

research.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
research.levelEvidence: Learning and memory; verbal feedback stored as episodic reflections across benchmark tasks
research.finding: Reusing verbal feedback from prior attempts improved performance on several tested decision, reasoning, and programming tasks.
research.impact: Watch feedback-linked episodes. Strengthen the rule that self-reflection cannot independently verify a claim or widen authority.
research.boundary: Benchmark feedback can be incomplete or wrong, and improvement does not establish durable correction. Next: when must feedback come from an independent test or human-owned source?
research.design: Conference benchmark study of stored verbal feedback

research.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
research.levelEvidence: Task and refinement; iterative generation, critique, and revision across seven tasks
research.finding: The same model's feedback-and-revision loop improved average task performance over one-step generation in the reported experiments.
research.impact: Watch inexpensive iterative refinement. Reject same-model critique as independent validation or durable learning.
research.boundary: The tasks emphasize bounded output quality, not external truth, correction survival, or workflow ownership. Next: where does same-model refinement stop helping or amplify a shared blind spot?
research.flags: same-model critique; task and judge dependence

research.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
research.levelEvidence: Memory architecture and evaluation; extraction, consolidation, retrieval, and graph-memory variants evaluated primarily on conversational benchmarks
research.finding: Selective memory extraction and consolidation can reduce context use and improve benchmark retrieval relative to several reported baselines.
research.impact: Watch selective consolidation as an implementation candidate only through a reproducible owning-system comparison. Reject vendor-reported benchmark gains as governance or deployment validation.
research.boundary: The paper is authored by the system's builders, uses benchmark and model-judge evaluation, and does not test repository custody, correction authority, or private-context isolation. Next: can an independent replay reproduce gains while preserving source evidence and deletion semantics?
research.design: Preprint builder evaluation of production memory system

research.title: Predict Responsibly: Improving Fairness and Accuracy by Learning to Defer
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; formal framework and experiments with synthetic decision makers
research.finding: Optimizing a model as part of a model-plus-decision-maker system can improve system accuracy or fairness relative to isolated rejection rules.
research.impact: Watch system-aware deferral as an evaluation concept. Reject synthetic gains as authority to automate routing.
research.boundary: The experiments largely simulate decision makers. Next: can prospective human evidence reproduce benefits under changing expertise and costs?
research.design: Conference formal framework with synthetic decision makers

research.title: Consistent Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; theoretical estimator plus benchmark experiments
research.finding: A classifier and rejector can be learned jointly from expert decisions so the system predicts or defers where each is expected to be stronger.
research.impact: Watch learned deferral regions. Reject past expert labels as permanent routing authority.
research.boundary: Structured labeled tasks do not capture accountability, drift, or private side information. Next: how quickly must deferral evidence expire after expert or distribution change?

research.title: Towards Unbiased and Accurate Deferral to Multiple Experts
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; multi-expert deferral framework with synthetic and crowdsourced evaluation
research.finding: Deferral can choose among experts with different strengths and biases, improving reported accuracy and fairness over tested baselines.
research.impact: Watch expertise-specific routing. Reject agent count or role labels as evidence of expertise.
research.boundary: Content moderation and constructed experts limit transfer. Next: what minimum current evidence qualifies an expert for a routing region?
research.design: Conference multi-expert framework with synthetic and crowd data

research.title: Calibrated Learning to Defer with One-vs-All Classifiers
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; theoretical calibration analysis and experiments
research.finding: A prior consistent deferral formulation was not calibrated for expert correctness; the proposed one-vs-all method produced calibrated probabilities in tested tasks.
research.impact: Strengthen calibration testing for deferral estimates. Reject consistency or accuracy alone as calibrated routing evidence.
research.boundary: Classification benchmarks do not validate open-ended delegation. Next: what calibration target is meaningful when correctness is delayed or multidimensional?

research.title: Improving Expert Predictions with Conformal Prediction
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; conformal decision-support design with simulated and real expert predictions
research.finding: Prediction sets can trade off misleading experts against task difficulty without requiring users to decide when to trust a single label.
research.impact: Watch bounded option sets and measured coverage. Reject forced-choice sets where the valid action may be abstention or escalation.
research.boundary: Multiclass prediction is narrower than open-ended work and experiments partly use simulated experts. Next: how should prediction-set logic expose missing-option risk?
research.design: Conference conformal support with simulated and real predictions
research.flags: bounded option sets; outcome observability required

research.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
research.levelEvidence: Task; preprint experiments using repeated debate among model instances
research.finding: Multiagent debate improved reported reasoning and factuality on selected benchmarks without model training.
research.impact: Watch debate as a task-specific candidate. Reject preprint benchmark gains as a general multi-agent advantage or independent verification.
research.boundary: Agents share model-family weaknesses and the work is not an owning-system field test. Next: when does debate outperform equal-cost sampling or one strong verifier?

research.title: Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate
research.levelEvidence: Task; debate experiments on translation and counter-intuitive arithmetic
research.finding: Debate increased divergence relative to self-reflection on tested tasks, but gains required controlled interaction and model judges were not always fair across different agents.
research.impact: Watch bounded disagreement and stopping rules. Reject the judge agent as neutral by default.
research.boundary: Two benchmark families do not establish durable workflow value. Next: how should judge bias and debate cost be measured prospectively?
research.flags: narrow tasks; judge bias and degeneration

research.title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for Mind Exploration of Large Scale Language Model Society
research.levelEvidence: Workflow; role-playing framework and instruction-following studies
research.finding: Inception prompting and role assignment can sustain autonomous agent conversations and enable study of cooperative behavior.
research.impact: Watch role-scoped communication as implementation evidence. Reject sustained conversation as task success or governance.
research.boundary: Generated tasks and conversational studies do not compare against the best single-agent baseline. Next: which role boundaries add unique information rather than duplicated language?
research.flags: generated tasks; sustained conversation is not success

research.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
research.levelEvidence: Workflow; software-agent framework with role-specific artifacts and benchmarks
research.finding: Encoding standard operating procedures into role-specific intermediate artifacts can structure multi-agent software generation.
research.impact: Watch typed intermediate artifacts. Reject simulated software-company roles as proof of real team capability.
research.boundary: Benchmarks and generated projects do not establish maintainability, security, or cost benefit in an owned repository. Next: which artifacts improve an equal-cost code task under independent tests?

research.title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
research.levelEvidence: Workflow; chat-chain software framework with role-based design, coding, and testing
research.finding: Structured role conversations and communicative clarification can produce software artifacts across staged development tasks.
research.impact: Watch explicit clarification and phase artifacts. Reject role play or generated code as evidence of production quality.
research.boundary: Evaluation does not establish superiority on mature private repositories. Next: does communicative clarification reduce defects more than direct requirements repair?
research.flags: generated software tasks; production transfer absent

research.title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
research.levelEvidence: Task and workflow; multi-agent framework evaluated on collaborative tasks and simulations
research.finding: Stage-based recruitment, decision, execution, and evaluation make agent-team composition configurable and expose emergent behaviors.
research.impact: Watch stage-specific orchestration. Reject emergence as benefit, safety, or authority.
research.boundary: Simulation and benchmark outcomes do not validate cross-repository professional work. Next: which stage can be removed without reducing outcome quality?
research.flags: emergence and simulation outcomes; limited governance

research.title: A Dynamic LLM-Powered Agent Network for Task-Oriented Agent Collaboration
research.levelEvidence: Task; dynamic team selection and communication experiments
research.finding: Selecting agents and stopping communication dynamically improved reported reasoning and code benchmarks relative to fixed collaboration baselines.
research.impact: Watch adaptive team size and early stopping. Reject agent-importance scores as human authority or universal expertise.
research.boundary: Benchmark contribution scores may not transfer across tasks, versions, or repositories. Next: can dynamic selection beat one agent under equal cost and unseen tasks?

research.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
research.levelEvidence: Memory and task; retrieval-plus-generation models evaluated on knowledge-intensive benchmarks
research.finding: Combining parametric generation with explicit non-parametric retrieval improved several knowledge tasks and made source updates and provenance more tractable than parametric memory alone.
research.impact: Strengthen source-linked retrieval. Reject retrieval as proof that the generated claim follows from or faithfully represents the source.
research.boundary: Wikipedia benchmarks do not cover repository authority, correction, or deletion. Next: what evidence binds each durable claim to retrieved source spans and version?
research.flags: Wikipedia tasks; retrieval is not entailment

research.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
research.levelEvidence: Retrieval; dual-encoder dense retrieval evaluated across open-domain QA datasets
research.finding: Learned dense retrieval substantially improved top-20 retrieval accuracy over a strong BM25 baseline on the tested QA datasets.
research.impact: Watch dense retrieval as a candidate index. Reject benchmark recall as governance, freshness, or answer correctness.
research.boundary: Open-domain QA differs from versioned repository evidence. Next: when should lexical, dense, and structural retrieval be combined?
research.flags: open-domain QA; recall is not answer validity

research.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
research.levelEvidence: Memory and task; controlled long-context QA and key-value retrieval experiments
research.finding: Models often used relevant information less reliably when it appeared in the middle of long contexts, even when the context fit the advertised window.
research.impact: Strengthen position-robust context tests and retrieval. Reject context-window size as effective-memory evidence.
research.boundary: Tested models and context layouts will age. Next: which current models remain position-sensitive on repository-derived evidence?
research.flags: model and layout sensitivity; synthetic key-value task

research.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
research.levelEvidence: Retrieval and generation; adaptive retrieval and critique evaluated across tasks
research.finding: Learned reflection tokens enabled on-demand retrieval and source critique, improving reported quality and factuality over several baselines.
research.impact: Watch retrieval gating and evidence critique. Reject self-critique as independent source validation.
research.boundary: Training and benchmarks do not test repository custody or correction authority. Next: what external check is required before critique changes durable memory?
research.design: Conference adaptive retrieval and self-critique benchmarks
research.flags: learned critique is not independent validation

research.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
research.levelEvidence: Retrieval and memory; hierarchical clustering and summarization evaluated on long-document tasks
research.finding: Recursive summaries can support retrieval across different abstraction levels and improve several long-document benchmarks.
research.impact: Watch hierarchical retrieval for global and local questions. Reject generated summaries as source truth.
research.boundary: Summaries can omit or distort details and the tests do not cover correction survival. Next: how can every abstraction retain auditable links to leaf evidence and invalidation events?
research.flags: generated summaries may distort leaf evidence

research.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
research.levelEvidence: Retrieval and memory; graph retrieval evaluated on multi-hop QA
research.finding: A knowledge graph plus Personalized PageRank improved reported multi-hop retrieval quality and efficiency over selected RAG baselines.
research.impact: Watch graph retrieval for cross-document association. Reject biological analogy or QA gains as governed-memory validation.
research.boundary: Benchmark graphs do not establish provenance, source precedence, deletion, or access control. Next: how should graph edges inherit source authority and tombstones?
research.flags: multi-hop QA; biological analogy; no tombstones

research.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
research.levelEvidence: Retrieval and corpus synthesis; graph indexing and community summaries evaluated on global sensemaking questions
research.finding: Graph-based community summaries improved reported comprehensiveness and diversity over conventional RAG for global questions over large corpora.
research.impact: Watch global-versus-local retrieval modes. Reject model-generated graph structure or summaries as canonical repository truth.
research.boundary: This is a builder-authored preprint with model-based evaluation. Next: can independent evaluators reproduce gains while tracing each synthesis claim to versioned sources?
research.design: Preprint builder evaluation of graph summarization

research.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking
research.levelEvidence: Interaction and workflow; survey of 319 knowledge workers covering 936 reported GenAI work examples
research.finding: Higher confidence in GenAI was associated with less reported critical-thinking enactment and effort, while confidence in one's own ability was associated with more. Critical work shifted toward verification, integration, and stewardship.
research.impact: Strengthen visible verification and human-owned synthesis. Watch cognitive-effort displacement.
research.boundary: Self-reported associations do not establish causal skill loss. Next: which observable review behaviors preserve critical engagement without adding performative friction?
research.design: Conference self-report survey of knowledge workers

research.title: Human-AI teaming in healthcare: 1 + 1 > 2?
research.levelEvidence: Task and interaction; reliability analysis of 52 empirical clinical studies
research.finding: Medical AI can augment clinicians, but full complementarity was uncommon. Concurrent review of cases and AI output outperformed sequential review, and junior clinicians benefited more than senior clinicians.
research.impact: Watch interaction order and expertise as contextual variables. Reject a universal handoff sequence.
research.boundary: Safety-critical clinical evidence cannot prescribe a general operating protocol. Next: when should a low-consequence workflow compare independent and concurrent review, while retaining an auditable human decision?
research.design: Journal reliability analysis of 52 clinical studies

research.title: Towards a Theory of Longitudinal Trust Calibration in Human-Robot Teams
research.levelEvidence: Team and interaction; integrative longitudinal trust model
research.finding: Trust calibration develops over time with work agreements, outcomes, and team dynamics rather than from a single explanation or score.
research.impact: Strengthen versioned work agreements and time-varying calibration. Reject one-time trust assessment.
research.boundary: The proposed model is theoretical and HRI-focused. Next: which events should update or invalidate a recorded reliance judgment?

research.title: Toward Quantifying Trust Dynamics: How People Adjust Their Trust After Moment-to-Moment Interaction With Automation
research.levelEvidence: Interaction; 75 participants completing 40 aided recognition trials
research.finding: Failures reduced trust more than successes increased it, and adjustments also reflected outcome bias and contrast with the participant's own result.
research.impact: Strengthen event-sequence reliance measurement. Reject one post-task trust snapshot as a sufficient account of collaboration.
research.boundary: The task was bounded image recognition and trust was self-reported after each trial. Next: which behavioral measures capture dynamic reliance without requiring intrusive continuous surveys?

research.title: Measuring Transactive Memory Systems in the Field
research.levelEvidence: Team and workflow; scale development and validation across laboratory and field teams
research.finding: Specialization, credibility, and coordination are separable dimensions of a transactive memory system and relate to team performance.
research.impact: Watch the three dimensions as evaluation prompts. Reject importing the human-team scale as an AI score.
research.boundary: The scale was validated for human teams, not agents or repositories. Next: which trace evidence can operationalize each dimension without anthropomorphism?
research.design: Journal scale development and laboratory-field validation
research.flags: human-team self-report scale; direct transfer rejected

research.title: Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams
research.levelEvidence: Team and organization; field study of 51 work teams
research.finding: Psychological safety was associated with learning behavior, which mediated team performance in the studied setting.
research.impact: Watch safe correction and escalation as human-workflow conditions. Reject interface affordances as proof that people feel safe to challenge outputs.
research.boundary: One organizational setting does not establish causality across AI-assisted work. Next: how can an evaluation detect suppressed disagreement without collecting sensitive free text?
research.design: Journal field study of 51 work teams

research.title: The Out-of-the-Loop Performance Problem and Level of Control in Automation
research.levelEvidence: Task and control; laboratory comparison of automation levels
research.finding: Higher automation reduced situation awareness and failure-recovery performance, while active participation moderated the loss.
research.impact: Strengthen active-review and reentry tests. Reject routine success as evidence of takeover readiness.
research.boundary: The controlled navigation task predates generative systems. Next: which active participation preserves readiness without erasing useful automation gains?

research.title: Expanding Explainability: Towards Social Transparency in AI Systems
research.levelEvidence: Organization and interaction; interviews with 29 AI users and practitioners using a speculative scenario
research.finding: Explanations can include who used the system, what they decided, and why, not only model internals, making organizational context visible.
research.impact: Watch social transparency as a trace-design candidate. Reject social precedent as authority or truth.
research.boundary: Interview and speculative evidence does not validate the proposed design. Next: which social context aids accountability without exposing private content or normalizing past errors?
research.flags: small qualitative sample; proposed design not deployed

research.title: Collaborative Intelligence: Humans and AI Are Joining Forces
research.levelEvidence: Organization and workflow; reported study of 1,500 companies plus organizational examples
research.finding: Human and machine strengths can complement each other, but value depends on redesigning work around collaboration rather than adding AI to an unchanged process.
research.impact: Strengthen complementarity and workflow redesign. No new principle.
research.boundary: This is organizational evidence, not proof of durable cross-session protocols. Next: what makes a redesigned workflow persist after participants or models change?

research.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Information Systems Research: A Systematic Literature Review and Future Research Directions
research.levelEvidence: Interaction, organization, and ecosystem; systematic review of 137 articles
research.finding: The literature converges on redefined human-machine relationships, interaction design, and organizational-societal implications. It still lacks longitudinal evidence, unified evaluation frameworks, and sufficient theoretical grounding.
research.impact: Strengthen the collaborative frame. Watch evaluation and longitudinal continuity as research debt, not claimed contributions.
research.boundary: A literature gap does not prove this repository fills it. Next: what evaluation scheme can compare collaboration quality without collapsing unlike contexts into one score?
research.flags: review quality not fully appraised; broad construct variation

research.title: Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance
research.levelEvidence: Interaction and decision; multidisciplinary review and conceptual model
research.finding: Trust affects reliance when full understanding is impractical, but the design goal is appropriate reliance calibrated to context and automation performance, not maximum trust.
research.impact: Strengthen calibrated reliance and evidence display. Reject confidence or user acceptance as sufficient evidence of safe collaboration.
research.boundary: The review predates current generative systems. Next: which observable behaviors show appropriate reliance when outputs and system capability change between runs?

research.title: Humans and Automation: Use, Misuse, Disuse, Abuse
research.levelEvidence: Interaction and organization; multidisciplinary conceptual review
research.finding: Overreliance, underuse, and inappropriate automation imposed by designers or managers are distinct failure modes rather than one trust problem.
research.impact: Strengthen separate reliance, disuse, and designer-authority checks. Reject adoption rate as evidence of appropriate collaboration.
research.boundary: The framework predates modern generative systems and supplies categories rather than a deployment test. Next: which observable workflow events distinguish justified nonuse from harmful disuse?

research.title: Trust in Automation: Integrating Empirical Evidence on Factors That Influence Trust
research.levelEvidence: Interaction; systematic review of empirical research published from 2002 through June 2013
research.finding: Trust is shaped by dispositional, situational, and learned factors, so a single end-state trust measure hides materially different causes.
research.impact: Strengthen layered trust evidence. Reject trust as a unitary score or direct proxy for appropriate reliance.
research.boundary: The review is broad but largely predates current generative assistants. Next: which layers predict actual reliance under changing model and task conditions?
research.design: Journal systematic review of trust evidence
research.flags: evidence ends in 2013; trust constructs vary

research.title: Trusting Automation: Designing for Responsivity and Resilience
research.levelEvidence: Interaction and recovery; narrative review and conceptual synthesis
research.finding: Trustworthy joint activity depends on responding to changing situations and recovering from mismatches, not only on initial calibration or reliability.
research.impact: Strengthen responsivity and recovery as separate protocol outcomes. Reject static trust calibration as sufficient continuity evidence.
research.boundary: This is a conceptual synthesis, not a controlled evaluation of a generative workflow. Next: which traces show that a participant noticed, communicated, and recovered from a changed situation?
research.design: Journal narrative review and conceptual synthesis

research.title: Automation Bias: A Systematic Review of Frequency, Effect Mediators, and Mitigators
research.levelEvidence: Decision and safety; systematic review of 74 studies selected from 13,821 records
research.finding: Automation bias appeared across settings, while its frequency and mitigation depended on task, user, workload, accountability, training, and interface design.
research.impact: Strengthen verification and accountability design. Reject alerts, confidence displays, or explanations as universal mitigations.
research.boundary: Much of the evidence concerns clinical or legacy decision support and reporting was heterogeneous. Next: which mitigations transfer to open-ended generative work without excessive burden?
research.design: Journal systematic review of automation bias

research.title: Grounding in Communication
research.levelEvidence: Interaction; theory and prior empirical work on conversational grounding
research.finding: Participants coordinate by establishing enough mutual understanding for the current purpose, with grounding costs shaped by the communication medium.
research.impact: Strengthen explicit grounding checks at handoff boundaries. Reject transcript volume as proof of common ground.
research.boundary: Human communication theory does not validate an AI protocol. Next: which observable acknowledgement and repair signals show sufficient grounding without adding excessive process?
research.design: Book chapter theory and empirical synthesis
research.flags: human communication; medium and task transfer

research.title: Measuring Team Knowledge
research.levelEvidence: Team; methodological review of team-knowledge measurement
research.finding: Team knowledge includes both shared and distributed structures, so individual knowledge aggregation can miss coordination-relevant organization.
research.impact: Strengthen separate tests for common ground and distributed expertise. Reject one pooled knowledge measure.
research.boundary: Measurement methods are task-sensitive and human-team focused. Next: which representation preserves specialization while still testing shared constraints?
research.design: Journal methodological review of team knowledge

research.title: Ironies of Automation
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and control; foundational analysis of automated process supervision
research.finding: Automation can leave people responsible for rare, difficult failures while reducing the practice and information needed to intervene effectively.
research.impact: Strengthen recovery-readiness and skill-retention tests. Reject nominal takeover authority without practiced capability.
research.boundary: Industrial process control differs from generative knowledge work. Next: what low-cost rehearsal shows that a human can actually recover a current workflow?
research.design: Journal foundational analysis of automated supervision

research.title: How in the World Did We Ever Get into That Mode? Mode Error and Awareness in Supervisory Control
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and control; analysis of mode awareness in supervisory systems
research.finding: Flexible automation modes create new monitoring demands and failures when operators cannot determine the active mode or its implications.
research.impact: Strengthen visible mode, authority, and routing state. Reject hidden transitions among agent or approval modes.
research.boundary: Aviation evidence does not prescribe a software interface. Next: which state changes require persistent display and which can remain in trace evidence?
research.flags: supervisory-control domain; no current agent trial

research.title: From Here to Autonomy: Lessons Learned From Human-Automation Research
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and system; synthesis of automation and autonomy evidence
research.finding: Reliable autonomy can still reduce situation awareness and make exception handling harder, so reliability and oversight readiness are distinct.
research.impact: Strengthen readiness and exception-recovery measures. Reject reliability alone as an autonomy-widening criterion.
research.boundary: The synthesis emphasizes safety-critical domains. Next: what proportional evidence is enough for low-consequence knowledge work?
research.design: Journal synthesis of automation and autonomy evidence

research.title: Human Performance Consequences of Stages and Levels of Automation: An Integrated Meta-Analysis
research.levelEvidence: Task and workflow; meta-analysis of 18 experiments
research.finding: Higher automation improved routine performance and workload but reduced situation awareness and failure performance, especially across the analysis-to-action-selection boundary.
research.impact: Strengthen function-specific benefit and recovery measurement. Reject one global automation level.
research.boundary: The studies vary and mostly predate LLM systems. Next: do the same tradeoffs appear when generative agents move from analysis to consequential action?

research.title: A Meta-Analysis of Factors Affecting Trust in Human-Robot Interaction
research.levelEvidence: Interaction; meta-analysis of 29 empirical studies
research.finding: Robot performance and attributes were stronger trust predictors than environmental factors in the reviewed evidence.
research.impact: Strengthen performance-history evidence. Reject trust as appropriate reliance and anthropomorphic presentation as competence evidence.
research.boundary: Human-robot interaction differs from language-agent work and trust is not calibration. Next: which performance-history display improves decisions rather than only confidence?
research.flags: robot interaction; trust is not reliance

research.title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
research.levelEvidence: Interaction; synthesis, expert review, and validation across AI interaction scenarios
research.finding: Eighteen guidelines span initial use, regular interaction, failure, and change over time, emphasizing expectation setting, correction, feedback, and adaptation.
research.impact: Watch the guidelines as an interaction coverage checklist. Reject guideline presence as outcome validation.
research.boundary: Relevance ratings do not prove implementation benefit. Next: which guidelines materially improve the specific workflow under matched evaluation?
research.design: Conference synthesis, expert review, and scenario validation
research.flags: guideline coverage is not outcome evidence

research.title: Explanation in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Social Sciences
research.levelEvidence: Interaction; interdisciplinary literature review
research.finding: Human explanations are selective, contrastive, and social, so technically complete accounts may be poor explanations for a user's actual question.
research.impact: Strengthen question-specific explanation design. Reject exhaustive trace dumps as sufficient explanation.
research.boundary: A synthesis does not establish one best interface. Next: how should the requested contrast determine the evidence shown?
research.flags: selective synthesis; no single interface test

research.title: Human-Algorithm Collaboration: Achieving Complementarity and Avoiding Unfairness
research.levelEvidence: Task and decision; theoretical analysis of combined human-algorithm loss and fairness
research.finding: Complementarity is not always achievable, and lower average loss can conflict with fair distribution of benefit or increase group error disparities.
research.impact: Strengthen impossibility checks and subgroup outcomes. Reject average complementarity as sufficient benefit.
research.boundary: The model abstracts human behavior and task structure. Next: which empirical conditions reveal that a workflow cannot beat its better component?
research.design: Conference theoretical complementarity and fairness analysis
research.flags: modeled losses and groups; no open-ended workflow

research.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work: Human-AI Symbiosis in Organizational Decision Making
research.levelEvidence: Decision and organization; conceptual synthesis
research.finding: AI contributes analytical processing under complexity while humans retain holistic and intuitive strengths under uncertainty and equivocality.
research.impact: Strengthen human judgment under uncertainty. Add decision context to future reviews. No new principle.
research.boundary: Conceptual framing does not measure a deployed collaboration protocol. Next: how should a system recognize when uncertainty calls for human judgment rather than more model effort?

research.title: Ten Challenges for Making Automation a Team Player in Joint Human-Agent Activity
research.levelEvidence: Interaction and workflow; conceptual challenge framework grounded in joint-activity research
research.finding: Useful teammates must support coordination, common ground, mutual predictability, and direction rather than behave as isolated tools.
research.impact: Strengthen the protocol layer. Test whether handoffs expose enough status, intent, limits, and correction state for another participant to coordinate safely.
research.boundary: A challenge framework is not a validation of this repository's protocol. Next: which challenges can be turned into observable conformance checks across session and model changes?
research.flags: classical automation transfer; no protocol trial

research.title: A Model for Types and Levels of Human Interaction with Automation
research.levelEvidence: Task, decision, and action; conceptual automation taxonomy with evaluative criteria
research.finding: Automation can operate at information acquisition, analysis, decision selection, or action implementation, and each function can receive a different level of automation.
research.impact: Strengthen function-specific authority allocation. Reject one global autonomy level for a workflow or agent.
research.boundary: This is a pre-generative-AI model, not an empirical validation of a current system. Next: which function-level authority choices improve performance without weakening accountability or recovery?
research.flags: pre-LLM taxonomy; no direct authority trial

research.title: Transactive Memory: A Contemporary Analysis of the Group Mind
research.levelEvidence: Team and organization; conceptual synthesis of distributed remembering
research.finding: A group can coordinate knowledge through awareness of who knows what rather than by duplicating all information in every member.
research.impact: Strengthen source ownership and knowledge-location routing. Reject central copying as the default continuity strategy.
research.boundary: Human group-memory theory does not establish repository behavior. Next: how should source-location knowledge remain current when owners, tools, or artifacts change?

research.title: Is There a Big Five in Teamwork?
research.levelEvidence: Team; theoretical synthesis of teamwork research
research.finding: Teamwork depends on several interacting behaviors and coordinating mechanisms, including monitoring, backup, adaptability, shared mental models, communication, and trust.
research.impact: Watch the taxonomy as a coverage check for protocols. Reject direct transfer as a validated agent-team design.
research.boundary: This is a human-team synthesis with propositions rather than an AI intervention test. Next: which elements add predictive value beyond existing handoff, recovery, and correction measures?

research.title: Distributed Cognition: Toward a New Foundation for Human-Computer Interaction Research
research.levelEvidence: Workflow and environment; theoretical HCI framework
research.finding: Cognitive work is distributed across people, artifacts, and environments, so the whole functional system is the proper unit of analysis.
research.impact: Strengthen workflow-level evaluation and artifact traceability. Reject model-only performance as system evidence.
research.boundary: The framework is analytical, not a measured implementation result. Next: what minimum system boundary captures the people, repositories, tools, and external constraints that affect an outcome?

research.title: Human-Centered Explainable AI: From Algorithms to User Experiences
research.levelEvidence: Interaction; selective survey and conceptual synthesis
research.finding: Human-centered XAI should begin with user needs, test pitfalls, and evaluate experiences rather than selecting an explanation algorithm first.
research.impact: Strengthen goal-specific explanation evaluation. Reject explainability as a context-free property.
research.boundary: The paper is a survey chapter, not a deployment result. Next: which user goal and consequence should each explanation support?
research.design: Preprint selective survey and conceptual synthesis
research.flags: preprint; selective coverage; no direct outcome test

research.title: Formalizing Trust in Artificial Intelligence: Prerequisites, Causes and Goals of Human Trust in AI
research.levelEvidence: Interaction and theory; formal and sociological analysis
research.finding: Trust involves user vulnerability and expectations about an implicit or explicit contract; trust can be warranted or unwarranted depending on its cause.
research.impact: Strengthen explicit capability contracts and warranted-reliance evidence. Reject trust maximization as a goal.
research.boundary: The formalization does not supply a complete measurement instrument. Next: which observable contract violations should immediately narrow reliance?

research.title: Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence: Reliable, Safe and Trustworthy
research.levelEvidence: System and design; conceptual HCAI framework
research.finding: High human control and high automation are not mutually exclusive, and function-specific designs can avoid a single autonomy continuum.
research.impact: Strengthen function-specific control and automation. Reject one human-versus-machine slider.
research.boundary: The framework is conceptual rather than comparative evaluation. Next: which functions can raise automation while preserving meaningful control?
