claims.title: Collaboration benefit is conditional
claims.claim: Human-AI or multi-agent collaboration should be treated as beneficial only when it beats the best relevant individual or established-workflow baseline on the outcome that matters for the bounded task.
claims.profile: high / not fully appraised / high / contested / bounded / repeated
claims.nullCase: the cooperative condition does not beat the better baseline, or gains disappear when quality, cost, burden, or safety is included.
claims.nextTest: compare no-AI, one-agent, and cooperative modes on the same unseen work item with equal outcome definitions and observed cost.

claims.title: Evaluate stages and workflow, not only final output
claims.readerLabel: Check each step of the work
claims.claim: Generation, selection, review, correction, handoff, and closeout can have different owners and outcomes, so one final-output measure cannot establish collaboration quality.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / high / convergent / bounded / repeated
claims.nullCase: stage measures add no explanatory or corrective value beyond final outcome and only increase burden.
claims.nextTest: identify the stage at which an observed gain, failure, or correction entered the work.

claims.title: Appropriate reliance is behavioral and dynamic
claims.readerLabel: When to trust or question AI
claims.claim: Trust, adoption, confidence, explanation presence, and stated preference are not substitutes for observed appropriate reliance across changing outcomes.
claims.profile: high / not fully appraised / high / mixed / bounded / repeated
claims.nullCase: a stated-trust measure predicts correct acceptance, rejection, escalation, and correction as well as behavioral measures.
claims.nextTest: record acceptance, verification, override, escalation, and recovery after both correct and incorrect assistance.

claims.title: Collaboration process has a cost
claims.claim: Added roles, messages, explanations, and review steps can reduce quality, throughput, independence, or willingness to engage even when intended as safeguards.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / moderate / convergent / bounded / single-task
claims.nullCase: the protocol improves the named outcome with no material time, burden, or independence cost.
claims.nextTest: record messages, elapsed time, active work, review burden, and post-handoff independence.

claims.title: Capability is task and context specific
claims.claim: Model or agent capability should be represented for a current task region, participant population, tool configuration, and time period rather than as one provider-level property.
claims.profile: high / not fully appraised / high / mixed / bounded / repeated
claims.nullCase: one stable capability label predicts performance across the relevant task and version changes.
claims.nextTest: define pre-action task signals and invalidate them after material model, tool, prompt, policy, or data changes.

claims.title: Process traces improve failure attribution and recovery
claims.claim: Privacy-minimal stage, action, evidence, and recovery traces can expose failures that final success or failure hides.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / moderate / convergent / narrow / technical-only
claims.nullCase: the trace does not improve attribution, correction, or replay enough to justify its privacy and operational cost.
claims.nextTest: compare failure diagnosis with final-output evidence versus a redacted complete trace.

claims.title: Authority must be bound to function and consequence
claims.claim: Information acquisition, analysis, recommendation, decision, and action require separate authority boundaries; one agent-wide autonomy level is not sufficient.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / high / convergent / bounded / repeated
claims.nullCase: a single autonomy level preserves the same safety, clarity, and recovery across all functions.
claims.nextTest: evaluate each function separately and require action-time approval for consequential mutations.

claims.title: Prior evidence expires after material change
claims.claim: Reliance, delegation, compatibility, and workflow evidence must be revalidated after material changes to models, prompts, tools, policy, data, task, or participant expertise.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / moderate / convergent / bounded / repeated
claims.nullCase: the prior result remains calibrated after the named change.
claims.nextTest: maintain a change manifest and run a targeted replay before reusing prior routing evidence.

claims.title: Effective memory is broader than recall
claims.claim: Memory evaluation must separate retrieval, updates, abstention, temporal and causal reasoning, role, efficiency, capacity, provenance, correction, custody, isolation, and deletion.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / high / convergent / narrow / technical-only
claims.nullCase: recall or context-window performance predicts correction, authority, and deletion behavior in the owning system.
claims.nextTest: run a repository-derived memory exam with source precedence, correction survival, tombstones, isolation, and stale-context rejection.

claims.title: Grounding should be sufficient and privacy-minimal
claims.readerLabel: Use enough context with less private data
claims.claim: Participants need shared objective, constraints, ownership, and correction state, but do not need universal access to all source content.
claims.profile: low / not fully appraised / high / convergent / bounded / repeated
claims.nullCase: the compact grounding record does not reduce wrong-premise work or requires copying protected source content.
claims.nextTest: compare a bounded handoff packet with transcript-scale context on orientation accuracy, privacy exposure, and repair cost.

claims.title: Human authority requires visible mode and recovery readiness
claims.claim: Nominal takeover or review authority is not meaningful when mode, routing, or system state is hidden or the human cannot recover after routine automation.
claims.profile: low / not fully appraised / high / convergent / bounded / repeated
claims.nullCase: routine reliability alone predicts safe intervention and recovery.
claims.nextTest: expose current mode and run a safe reentry or stale-context drill.

claims.title: Explanation must target a named behavior
claims.claim: An explanation should be evaluated against a specified behavior, such as error detection, correction, escalation, or appropriate reliance, rather than confidence, preference, or explanation presence.
claims.profile: high / not fully appraised / high / contested / bounded / single-task
claims.nullCase: explanation presence alone improves the named behavior without increasing bias or burden.
claims.nextTest: predeclare one behavioral target and measure side effects.

claims.title: Deferral evidence must be calibrated and expiring
claims.readerLabel: Know when to hand work to a person
claims.claim: Routing to a person, model, or specialist is justified only for the current task region, expert, option coverage, and distribution, with abstention and escalation preserved.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / high / convergent / narrow / single-task
claims.nullCase: an uncalibrated or permanent routing rule performs as well after expert or distribution change.
claims.nextTest: create an expiring deferral record and test delayed, multidimensional, and disputed outcomes.

claims.title: Retrieval architecture must match the query
claims.readerLabel: Choose the right way to find information
claims.claim: Lexical, dense, adaptive, hierarchical, graph, and long-context approaches solve different retrieval problems and must preserve links to versioned leaf evidence.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / high / convergent / narrow / technical-only
claims.nullCase: one retrieval mode performs equivalently across local, global, temporal, update, and association queries while preserving governance.
claims.nextTest: compare retrieval modes on the same repository-derived query set with provenance and tombstone checks.

claims.title: Average quality can hide portfolio diversity loss
claims.claim: Repeated AI assistance can improve average item quality while reducing the diversity or resilience of the collective output portfolio.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / low / sparse / narrow / single-task
claims.nullCase: assisted and unassisted portfolios have equivalent diversity and downstream option value at matched quality.
claims.nextTest: measure semantic and strategic diversity across a repeated research or design portfolio.

claims.title: More agents are not a general advantage
claims.readerLabel: Use more agents only when they help
claims.claim: Additional agents should be added only when a task-specific, equal-cost comparison shows that decomposition, topology, or independent information improves the bounded outcome.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / moderate / contested / narrow / technical-only
claims.nullCase: multi-agent work consistently beats one strong agent under equal cost on unseen, nonparallel tasks.
claims.nextTest: use mature-repository holdouts, equal budgets, and an independent evaluator.

claims.title: Self-refinement is not independent verification
claims.claim: Reflection, critique, debate, or iterative revision by the same model family may improve an output but cannot independently verify a durable claim, correction, or authority change.
claims.profile: moderate / not fully appraised / moderate / convergent / bounded / technical-only
claims.nullCase: same-model critique detects material errors at the same rate as an independent source, tool, or reviewer.
claims.nextTest: compare same-model refinement with evidence-bound independent verification.
